questions.q: With what does Yahweh ask Job if he can draw out Leviathan?
questions.a: Yahweh asks Job if he can draw out Leviathan with a fishhook.

questions.q: What does God ask Job might happen if the fishermen were to catch Leviathan?
questions.a: He asks Job if the fishermen would bargain for Leviathan or divide him up to trade among the merchants.

questions.q: What will happen if a person puts his hand on Leviathan?
questions.a: It someone puts his hand on the Leviathan just once, he will remember the battle and do it no more.

questions.q: Since no one is fierce enough to dare stir Leviathan up, can anyone stand before Yahweh?
questions.a: No one dares to stir Leviathan up, so there is no one who can stand before Yahweh.

questions.q: How else does Yahweh describe Leviathan’s mouth?
questions.a: He says it is the doors of his face, ringed with teeth, which are a terror.

questions.q: How close are the scales on the back of Leviathan?
questions.a: One is so near to another that no air can come between them.

questions.q: How does Yahweh say Leviathan’s eyes are like?
questions.a: His eyes are like eyelids of the dawn, bright and glowing.

questions.q: What comes out of Leviathan’s mouth?
questions.a: Out of Leviathan’s mouth go flames and fiery sparks.

questions.q: What is the smoke from Leviathan’s nostrils like?
questions.a: It is like a boiling pot on a fire that has been fanned to be very hot.
His heart is as hard as a lower millstone.

questions.q: What do the mighty do when Leviathan raises himself up?
questions.a: They become afraid and draw back.

questions.q: What happens when a sword, spear, arrow or any pointed weapon strikes Leviathan?
What does Leviathan think of iron and bronze?
questions.a: He thinks of iron as if it were straw and bronze as if it were rotten wood.

questions.q: What kind of trail does Leviathan leave?
questions.a: He leaves a spreading trail in the mud as if he were a threshing sledge.

questions.q: What does he make the deep to do?
questions.a: He makes the deep to foam up like a boiling pot of water.

questions.q: Why does Leviathan have no equal on earth?
questions.a: He s has been made to live without fear.

commentary.text: —The description of the Leviathan, is yet further to convince Job of his own weakness, and of God's almighty power. Whether this Leviathan be a whale or a crocodile, is disputed. The Lord, having showed Job how unable he was to deal with the Leviathan, sets forth his own power in that mighty creature. If such language describes the terrible force of Leviathan, what words can express the power of God's wrath? Under a humbling sense of our own vileness, let us revere the Divine Majesty; take and fill our allotted place, cease from our own wisdom, and give all glory to our gracious God and Saviour. Remembering from whom every good gift cometh, and for what end it was given, let us walk humbly with the Lord.
